pr_body:
This PR fixes a failed test on Nucleo F429ZI board: tests/drivers/uart/uart_async_api/drivers.uart.async_api
This fix disables the data cache for this test as it is incompatible with the use of DMA.

Fixes #50554
pr_comments:
Closing this PR as this test is unstable and any minor modification is susceptible to make the test PASS or FAIL.
For example, a double call to the function `LL_FLASH_EnableDataCache();` makes the test PASS.

issue_context.title: Test uart async failed on Nucleo F429ZI
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The test `tests/drivers/uart/uart_async_api/drivers.uart.async_api` fails on Nucleo F429ZI with the following error
`Assertion failed at WEST_TOPDIR/zephyr/tests/drivers/uart/uart_async_api/src/test_uart_async.c:526: uart_async_write_abort_test_write_abort: (sent not equal to received)
Sent is not equal to received.`
comments:
After investigation, it appears that it is a case of unstable test.
A git bisect has shown that commit ad1d6d passes and following commit 32ad01 fails, but the only difference between the two is in the MAINTAINERS.yml file.
A simple modification of the error message (to display the number of bytes sent and received) makes the test PASS.
Similarly, a repetition of an instruction makes the test PASS.

@dcpleung One question about this specific test:
```
uart_async_write_abort_test_write_abort: (sent not equal to received) Sent is not equal to received.
```
If user aborts the on going transaction, the expectation is that the procedure stops. I don't think it is meaningful to ensure that the rx side received the exact number of bytes sent before the abort. To my view this test point is highly susceptible to make the test instable, as we can see on `nucleo_f429zi` target.
I would propose to rework this part of the test.

I think there's value in ensuring that we have received the same number of bytes that have already sent. Could you try adding some delay before the check? It is possible that the check was done before the driver initiated the receive callback.
not reproduced anymore since a while

review_comments: Please add a comment explaining what type of data cache is in place here.
